newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MSF worried about evacuation of Rwandan refugees.
newsitem.headline: MSF worried about evacuation of Rwandan refugees.

text.p: International relief group Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) protested on Sunday against rebel pressure to quickly evacuate Rwandan Hutu refugees from the camp in Biaro to the town of Kisangani in northeastern Zaire.

MSF (doctors without borders) said the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) was pressing international humanitarian agencies to evacuate the refugees to Kisangani within 10 days.

MSF said in a statement issued in Brussels it firmly opposed this, saying that hundreds of refugees in the Biaro camp some 42 kilometres south of Kinsangani were too weak to be transported and would probably not survive such a trip.
In addition, thousands were hiding in the forests and did not dare go to the camp for help because of persistent rumours about army intimidation.

"The refugees who will still be in the region after this time limit of ten days because they are too weak to walk or too frightened to come out of the forest, will they be left to their own fate?" the statement said.
"That is what MSF fears if the region south of Kisangani is closed for humanitarian organisations," it added, demanding that AFDL should guarantee free access for aid agencies to the area.
Every day the local Red Cross collected some 40 corpses in the camp, unable to do more, it said. Refugees were suffering from malnutrition, dehydration and exhaustion.
"It is of utmost importance to stabilise the medical situation of these refugees before transporting them to Kisangani," the MSF statement said.

MSF also expressed concern about the fate of thousands of refugees still reported missing. The group demanded that an independent human rights commission should immediately be admitted into the region to investigate rumours about massacres and intimidation.
There have been reports that rebel troops have mistreated Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire.
The Hutus are the rump of two million Rwandans who fled to Zaire after Tutsi rebels ended the Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994.
The head of Rwanda's repatriation commission said last week only 55,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees remained in Zaire and that a United Nations airlift would take nearly half of them home within ten days.
